note: RFC 1661 Section 2: "Frames received which don't comply with these rules MUST be treated as having an unrecognized Protocol." Rejudged after 83deb89129, which changed only the doc comment of TestRFC1661CompliantProtocolRecognized ('dropped' became a Protocol-Reject, matching the code). Low-octet rule: TestRFC1661NonCompliantProtocolTreatedUnrecognized sends 0xC020 and asserts no termination, exactly one Protocol-Reject naming 0xC020 and state Opened; the recorded mutant removes the final rejectUnsupportedProtocol return of handleFrame. High-octet rule: TestRFC1661ProtocolWithOddHighOctetTreatedUnrecognized sends 0xC121 and asserts one Protocol-Reject naming it, so no Echo-Reply, and state Opened. Transmit side: the same unit checks both parity bits on LCP, PAP, CHAP, IPCP, IPV6CP, IPv4 and IPv6, and the package's WriteFrame callers name LCP, PAP, CHAP and the NCP protocols; the one variable caller, session_run.go:2228, was judged earlier as writeCodeReject with ProtoLCP or ncpProto and was not re-traced here. TestRFC1661CompliantProtocolRecognized requires the Echo-Reply under 0xC021, so a blanket refusal goes red. Caveat on proof: the recorded break of the parity-constant positive panics rejectUnsupportedProtocol, which reddens the later half of the unit and never falsifies the constant loop; by reading, an even constant reaches t.Fatalf, but no record shows it.
